title: Left-infinite digits and the 3-adic topology
notes: \ru{3-адические числа (для школьников)}; infinitely many digits extend to the left, and the rules and topology are introduced by analogy.
statement: \(\mathbb Z_3=\varprojlim_k\mathbb Z/3^k\mathbb Z\). Each element has a unique expansion \(\sum_{j\geq0}a_j3^j\), \(a_j\in\{0,1,2\}\), convergent for \(|x|_3=3^{-v_3(x)}\). Addition and multiplication are compatible finite carry operations modulo \(3^k\); \(\mathbb Q_3=\mathbb Z_3[1/3]\). The digit construction first describes the ring of integers, not every element of the field without a finite right-hand tail.
reconstruction: The inverse limit, valuation and distinction between the integer ring and field make the informal construction precise.
fate: Classical arithmetic, already known before the seminar; \citet[Chs.~3--4]{gouvea2020padic} is a modern exposition, not the first publication.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The ternary expansions of minus one and one half
notes: The sums display \(\ldots2222=-1\) and \(\ldots11112=1/2\); the latter is obtained by multiplying by two and carrying.
statement: In \(\mathbb Z_3\), \(\sum_{j\geq0}2\cdot3^j=-1\) and \(2+\sum_{j\geq1}3^j=1/2\). Indeed the finite truncations are \(3^{k+1}-1\) and \((3^{k+1}+1)/2\); their errors tend to zero in the 3-adic norm. The displays are expansions in base three.
reconstruction: Finite-truncation verification is supplied here; no research novelty is claimed.
fate: These are elementary instances of the geometric-series calculation in the 3-adic ring; the modern reference is \citet[Ch.~4]{gouvea2020padic}. The finite-truncation identities also verify the notebook directly.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Decimal identifications and the nonfield of 10-adic integers
notes: The real expansion \(0.999\ldots=1\) is contrasted with a disconnected digit space. The last line says \ru{10-адические --- деления нет} and notes the absence of \(1/5\).
statement: The real value map from digit sequences to \([0,1]\) is continuous and identifies the familiar terminating/nonterminating pairs; its image is connected although its domain is totally disconnected. In contrast, \(\mathbb Z_{10}=\varprojlim_k\mathbb Z/10^k\mathbb Z\simeq\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_5\) by the Chinese remainder theorem. Its units are precisely the elements invertible modulo ten; \(5\) is not a unit, so \(1/5\notin\mathbb Z_{10}\). Division by units does exist.
reconstruction: The product-ring formulation and restriction of the phrase no division to nonunits are editorial precisifications.
fate: This is classical positional arithmetic. The prime-base setting is treated by \citet[Ch.~3]{gouvea2020padic}; the product description is the direct inverse-limit form of the Chinese remainder theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The spectral function of a positive elliptic realization
notes: \((Pu,u)\geq c(u,u)\), \(\widehat P=\int\lambda\,dE_\lambda\), and \(e(x,y,\lambda)\in C^\infty(\Omega\times\Omega)\) are introduced.
statement: Let \(P\) be a scalar elliptic differential operator of order \(m>0\) with smooth coefficients on a smooth manifold \(\Omega\), formally self-adjoint and bounded below by \(c>0\) on \(C_c^\infty\) for a fixed smooth positive density. For a self-adjoint realization \(\widehat P\geq c\), let \(E_\lambda=1_{(-\infty,\lambda]}(\widehat P)\). Its Schwartz kernel is the spectral function \(e(x,y,\lambda)\), smooth in the spatial variables locally in the interior for each finite \(\lambda\). Smoothness here does not mean continuity in the spectral parameter.
reconstruction: The density, self-adjoint realization, scalar ellipticity and interior restriction are restored from the identified source.
fate: The precise setup is already \citet[pp.~193--194]{hormander1968spectral}; received 7 May 1968, printed December 1968, before this exposition.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The local Weyl remainder
notes: The diagonal expression is \(\lambda^{-n/m}e(x,x,\lambda)-(2\pi)^{-n}\int_{p^0(x,\xi)<1}d\xi=O(\lambda^{-1/m})\).
statement: In the preceding setting, with real positive principal symbol \(p_m\), uniformly for \(x\) in each compact interior set, \[e(x,x,\lambda)=(2\pi)^{-n}\lambda^{n/m}\operatorname{vol}\{\xi:p_m(x,\xi)<1\}+O(\lambda^{(n-1)/m}).\] The cotangent measure is dual to the chosen base density.
reconstruction: The formula is a local estimate; boundary terms and uniformity to a boundary are not asserted.
fate: Exact match: \citet[Theorem~1.1]{hormander1968spectral}. The 1968 publication precedes Bleher\textquotesingle s talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Off-diagonal leading term
notes: The underlined phrase is \ru{Вне диагонали 0}.
statement: For fixed distinct interior points, the leading \(\lambda^{n/m}\) diagonal term disappears. In the local coordinate domain of the oscillatory formula, on compact subsets away from the diagonal, \(e(x,y,\lambda)=O(\lambda^{(n-1)/m})\); in particular \(\lambda^{-n/m}e(x,y,\lambda)\to0\). The unnormalized kernel is generally not zero.
reconstruction: Zero is read as zero leading normalized term. The notebook does not write this normalization in its short phrase.
fate: The relevant off-diagonal parametrix and estimate are in \citet[Theorem~5.1 and (5.4), p.~215]{hormander1968spectral}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Spherical harmonics and the spectral jump
notes: For the Laplacian on \(S^n\), the jump is written \((C_{n+k}^{k}-C_{n+k}^{k-2})/V_n\), with large multiplicities attributed to rotations.
statement: For the nonnegative Laplacian on the unit \(S^n\), \(n\geq1\), the eigenvalue \(\lambda_k=k(k+n-1)\) has multiplicity \[d_{n,k}=\binom{n+k}{k}-\binom{n+k-2}{k-2},\] with the second binomial zero for \(k<2\). Rotational invariance and integration over the sphere give the pointwise projector diagonal \(d_{n,k}/\operatorname{vol}(S^n)\). The upper index of the second binomial in the notebook must change.
reconstruction: The eigenvalue and correct binomial coefficient are supplied; the transcriptions faithfully preserve the erroneous second index.
fate: The example is analyzed in \citet[\S6]{hormander1968spectral}; the corrected formula also follows by subtracting the dimensions of homogeneous polynomials of degrees \(k\) and \(k-2\).
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Why a universal smaller unsmoothed remainder is impossible
notes: The jump has size \(\lambda^{(n-1)/2}\); the notes say one cannot write a term \(C\lambda^{(n-1)/2}\).
statement: For the sphere, \(d_{n,k}\sim2k^{n-1}/(n-1)!\) as \(k\to\infty\). A continuous approximation has the same limiting value on both sides of each jump, so at least one one-sided error is at least half that jump. Consequently an unsmoothed expansion with remainder \(o(\lambda^{(n-1)/2})\) is impossible, even after adding a fixed continuous term of that order. An \(O(\lambda^{(n-1)/2})\) bound remains valid.
reconstruction: The distinction between a big-O bound and a fixed second asymptotic coefficient is essential; the Russian abbreviated sentence does not deny the valid big-O estimate.
fate: Avakumovi\v{c}\textquotesingle s sharpness example is explicitly credited and proved in \citet[\S6]{hormander1968spectral}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Higher spectral terms after averaging
notes: The page asks for the next term of \(\lambda^{-1}\int_0^\lambda e(x,x,\nu)\,d\nu\), says this has not been done except for a square, and distinguishes obtaining subsequent terms from a formal asymptotic expansion.
statement:
For the positive elliptic \(P\) above, determine how many symbol-computable asymptotic terms are justified for the normalized Riesz means \[e^\alpha(x,x,\lambda)=\int_0^\lambda(1-
u/\lambda)^\alpha\,d_
u e(x,x,
u),\quad\alpha>0.\] For \(\alpha=1\) integration by parts gives the notebook	extquotesingle s average. If the leading Weyl coefficient is \(a_0(x)\), its leading averaged coefficient is \(m a_0(x)/(m+n)\). A fixed smoothing order does not automatically yield an arbitrarily accurate expansion.
reconstruction: The smoothing parameter and exact quantifier are editorial. The incorrect leading coefficient and the assertion of no existing work are not adopted.
fate: Already addressed in \citet[Theorem~4.5 and pp.~215--216]{hormander1968spectral}, with remainder order \(O(\lambda^{(n-1-\alpha)/m})\) after the appropriate finite expansion. The antecedent was circulated at the November 1966 Belfer conference and translated in 1968: \citet{hormander1968riesz}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the general Riesz-mean framework was already available by 1968. Unsmoothed full expansions are obstructed by spectral jumps; no unresolved problem is inferred from this wording.

title: The trace-formula reading pointer
notes: The notes recommend Dikii in UMN, dated 1957, and an earlier Gelfand work, dated 1954, on traces.
statement: This is a bibliographical pointer to regularized spectral traces, not a recorded trace identity. No boundary conditions, potential, summation prescription or operator pair are specified; a unique theorem cannot be reconstructed from the pointer alone.
fate: The identifiable UMN review is \citet{dikii1958traces}, published in 1958, pp.~111--143. The Gelfand pointer is too abbreviated to identify one publication without a conjectural attribution.
present_status: As of November 2026: the review is identified and its date corrected; no independent mathematical question is recoverable from the remaining pointer.

title: Reduction to a first-order pseudodifferential root
statement: On a closed manifold, for a positive invertible classical scalar elliptic \(P\) of order \(m\), spectral functional calculus defines \(A=P^{1/m}\), a classical pseudodifferential operator of order one with principal symbol \(p_m^{1/m}\). Its full symbol has a homogeneous asymptotic expansion away from the zero section. On a general open manifold the corresponding assertion is used microlocally in the interior.
reconstruction: Closedness and invertibility give a clean global version; a local statement suffices for the notes.
fate: Already used in \citet[p.~195]{hormander1968spectral}, citing Seeley\textquotesingle s complex-power construction. It is not a new method invented in Bleher\textquotesingle s talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Half-wave evolution and propagation of singularities
notes: \(G(t)=e^{itA}\), \((i\partial_t+A)G(t)=0\), \(G(0)=I\); the generalized Huygens principle is described as finite-speed propagation of singularities.
statement: For self-adjoint \(A\), \(G(t)=e^{itA}\) is unitary and satisfies the displayed equation on its operator domain. When \(A\) is a real-principal-type first-order elliptic pseudodifferential operator, its short-time kernel is microlocally associated with the Hamiltonian flow, with sign determined by this evolution convention. Propagation of wavefront singularities is asserted, not compact support propagation for an arbitrary nonlocal operator.
reconstruction: The qualification concerns singularities, which is exactly the Russian noun; finite speed of the entire support would be stronger and generally false.
fate: The half-wave reduction and geometrical-optics construction are \citet[pp.~195--196 and \S3]{hormander1968spectral}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: A short-time phase and transport amplitude
notes: The ansatz has phase \(\psi(x,y,\xi)-t a_1(y,\xi)\), \(\psi=(x-y,\xi)+O(|x-y|^2|\xi|)\), an amplitude expansion and a smoothing remainder.
statement: Locally choose a homogeneous phase solving the appropriate eikonal equation and construct a classical amplitude by transport equations so that the oscillatory integral solves the half-wave equation modulo a smooth kernel for sufficiently small \(|t|\). In the local normal form used here, \(\psi\) satisfies \(a_1(x,d_x\psi)=a_1(y,\xi)\); signs are adjusted if the Fourier exponential is reversed. The condition \(\psi=(x-y)\cdot\xi+O(|x-y|^2|\xi|)\) alone would not determine a valid parametrix.
reconstruction: The omitted eikonal and transport conditions supply the substantive hypotheses of the ansatz.
fate: Exact construction: \citet[\S3, especially the phase and transport equations]{hormander1968spectral}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Fourier cutoff, smoothed spectral density and the Tauberian step
notes: The smooth error \(E-Q\) is multiplied by \(\widehat\varrho(t)\); P000275 gives the convolution \(\int\varrho(\lambda-\mu)\,de(x,y,\mu)\) and defines \(R=\mathcal F^{-1}(q\widehat\varrho)\). A Marchenko Tauberian theorem is mentioned.
statement: Choose \(\widehat\varrho\in C_c^\infty((-\varepsilon,\varepsilon))\). Fourier transformation of the localized smooth error is rapidly decreasing in the spectral variable. The remaining term is an oscillatory integral with amplitude \(R\). The diagonal spectral measure is positive; this positivity and a suitable cutoff permit a Tauberian estimate recovering the unsmoothed local counting bound. A displayed difference on P000275 is therefore a rapidly decreasing error, not an exact equality to zero.
reconstruction: The order of the error, support of the cutoff and role of diagonal positivity are supplied explicitly.
fate: The relevant estimates and Tauberian recovery are in \citet[\S4]{hormander1968spectral}; the notebook\textquotesingle s named Tauberian attribution is not needed to identify a separate theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: A pair without a common isotropic vector has a definite combination
notes: If two quadratic forms are not simultaneously zero, rotate their pair of values so that one form is positive definite.
statement: Let \(A,B\) be Hermitian \(n\times n\) complex matrices. If \(x^*Ax=x^*Bx=0\) implies \(x=0\), there exist real \(a,b\) with \(aA+bB>0\). For real symmetric matrices with the hypothesis tested only on real vectors, an additional dimension qualification is needed; the unrestricted two-dimensional version is false.
reconstruction: The complex field and exclusion of the zero vector are restored. A real counterexample is \(A=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), \(B=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\): the forms have no common nonzero real zero, while every nonzero real combination is indefinite.
fate: The named paper is \citet[pp.~545--548]{auyeung1969sphere}, published February 1969, before the talk. Its publisher contents and bibliographic identity were checked; the original article was not accessible. The exact complex assertion is independently readable in \citet[\S1, (1.1)]{guohighamtisseur2008arc}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The arc of normalized values and separation
notes: The value pair \((x^*Ax,x^*Bx)\) is normalized; the resulting direction runs through no more than a semicircle.
statement: For a complex Hermitian definite pair, \(W(A+iB)=\{x^*(A+iB)x:\|x\|=1\}\) is compact and convex and excludes zero. Strict separation from zero puts its directions in a closed arc of length strictly less than \(\pi\). The separating real functional gives a positive definite combination.
reconstruction: Compact numerical-range separation supplies the missing strictness; containment in an arbitrary closed semicircle alone would yield only semidefiniteness.
fate: This is the geometric method associated with \citet{auyeung1969sphere}. The arc statement and its use in definite-pair algorithms are explicit in \citet[Lemma~2.1 and \S2]{guohighamtisseur2008arc}; that 2008 preprint is a later exposition and development, not the date of the theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Simultaneous diagonalization by congruence
notes: The forms can be simultaneously reduced \ru{к сумме квадратов}.
statement: Under the definite-pair hypothesis, there is an invertible complex \(S\) with \(S^*AS\) and \(S^*BS\) both real diagonal. Choose \(C=aA+bB>0\), use \(C^{-1/2}\) to make \(C\) the identity, then diagonalize the other Hermitian member by a unitary matrix. The diagonal coefficients of the original forms need not all be nonnegative.
reconstruction: The displayed construction is an editorial verification of a standard consequence, not a claim that this proof was written in the notebook.
fate: The precise congruence convention is also spelled out by \citet[p.~81]{auyeung1970diagonalization}. The elementary reduction explains the conclusion of the February 1969 paper without inferring positivity of both forms.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Operators as linear relations
notes: The graph is written \((y,x)\), \(y=Ax\); a more general relation is \(\alpha\subset M\oplus H\).
statement: Let \(H\) be a complex Hilbert space. A linear relation is a linear subspace \(\alpha\subset H\oplus H\), written in output--input order \((y,x)\). A closed operator has closed graph \(\alpha=\{(Ax,x):x\in\operatorname{Dom}A\}\); a general closed relation may be multivalued and need not have dense domain.
reconstruction: Linearity, and closedness where spectral conclusions require it, are added to the bare word set. An arbitrary subset is not the relevant notion of relation.
fate: This is the framework of \citet[\S\S1--2]{davis1968shell}, already published in 1968.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

statement:

title: The indicatrix cone
notes: \(\{(\|Ax\|^2,x^*Ax,\|x\|^2):x\ne0\}\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb C\times\mathbb R\) is called a cone.
statement: For a nonzero linear relation \(\alpha\), its indicatrix is the set of triples \((\|y\|^2,\langle y,x\rangle,\|x\|^2)\) over nonzero \((y,x)\in\alpha\). Scaling the pair scales the triple by a positive real number. Every triple satisfies \(|\langle y,x\rangle|^2\leq\|y\|^2\|x\|^2\).
reconstruction: The relation version makes the operator formula compatible with the subsequent projective action.
fate: Exact construction in \citet[Definition~1.1 and the preceding normalization]{davis1968shell}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The shell in the closed unit ball
notes: The convenient section is \((\xi,h)=(2x^*Ax,(\|Ax\|^2-\|x\|^2))/(\|Ax\|^2+\|x\|^2)\), with \(|\xi|^2+h^2\leq1\).
statement: Normalize each nonzero pair \((y,x)\in\alpha\) by \(t=\|y\|^2+\|x\|^2\): \[s(\alpha)=\{(2\langle y,x\rangle/t,(\|y\|^2-\|x\|^2)/t)\}.\] Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(s(\alpha)\subset\{(\xi,h):|\xi|^2+h^2\leq1\}\). This set need not be closed; closure must be written explicitly when used.
reconstruction: Set braces, quantification and the distinction between the shell and its closure repair the abbreviated notation.
fate: This is \citet[Definition~1.1]{davis1968shell}, with equivalent stereographic coordinates.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Boundary points recover eigenvalues
notes: An eigenvector is obtained when the shell point belongs to the sphere; the eigenvalue is related by stereographic projection.
statement: For bounded \(A\), put \(\tau(\lambda)=(2\lambda/(1+|\lambda|^2),(|\lambda|^2-1)/(1+|\lambda|^2))\). Then \(s(A)\cap S^2=\tau(\sigma_p(A))\). Equality in Cauchy--Schwarz forces \(Ax=\lambda x\), and conversely. The north pole represents the infinite value for general multivalued relations, not an eigenvalue of a bounded operator.
reconstruction: The bounded-operator statement avoids conflating eigenvalues with approximate eigenvalues or the extra point at infinity.
fate: Exact match with \citet[Theorem~2.2]{davis1968shell}; Theorem~2.3 separately treats the approximate point spectrum using closure.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Height bounds encode an upper norm bound
notes: If the shell does not go above \((a^2-1)/(a^2+1)\), then \(a\) is the norm.
statement: For \(a\geq0\) and bounded \(A\), \[\|A\|\leq a\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\leq\frac{a^2-1}{a^2+1}\text{ for every }(\xi,h)\in s(A).\] Equality \(\|A\|=a\) holds when \(a\) is the least such bound; the supremum need not be attained.
reconstruction: The notebook\textquotesingle s asserted equality is replaced by the correct inequality and a separate minimality condition.
fate: The shell formulation of the norm is in \citet[\S1 and Definition~7.1]{davis1968shell}. It also follows by solving the normalized ratio for \(\|Ax\|^2/\|x\|^2\).
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Fractional linear transformations of relations
notes: \(\mu(\lambda)=(a\lambda+b)/(c\lambda+d)\), \(ad-bc\ne0\), acts by \((y,x)\mapsto(ay+bx,cy+dx)\).
statement: For complex \(a,b,c,d\) with \(ad-bc\ne0\), this invertible bounded block transformation sends a closed linear relation to a closed linear relation \(\mu(\alpha)\). If \(A\) is bounded and \(cA+dI\) is boundedly invertible, the transformed graph is the graph of \((aA+bI)(cA+dI)^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The inverse condition and identity operators are made explicit; the relation construction continues to exist when an operator formula does not.
fate: Exact relation calculus in \citet[\S5]{davis1968shell}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Möbius equivariance of the shell
notes: Theorem 1 states \(s(\mu(\alpha))=\varrho_\mu(s(\alpha))\).
statement: Act on the positive Hermitian Gram matrix \(G=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\|y\|^2&\langle y,x\rangle\\\langle x,y\rangle&\|x\|^2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) by \(G\mapsto M G M^*\), \(M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), then divide by its trace. The resulting projective transformation \(\varrho_\mu\) of the closed ball satisfies the notebook\textquotesingle s identity and restricts on the boundary to stereographic conjugation of \(\mu\).
reconstruction: The Gram-matrix construction defines the otherwise unnamed ball transformation; it is not an arbitrary analytic map of a three-dimensional ball.
fate: This is \citet[Theorem~5.1]{davis1968shell}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Spectral sets and the rational functional calculus
notes: \(X\) is spectral when every rational \(f\) with \(f(X)\subset D\) satisfies \(\|f(A)\|\leq1\).
statement: In the standard bounded-operator formulation, a closed set \(X\subset\mathbb C\) containing \(\sigma(A)\) is a spectral set if \(\|f(A)\|\leq\sup_X|f|\) for every rational function with poles off \(X\). The unit-disk formulation is equivalent by rescaling. For general relations and subsets of the Riemann sphere, use Davis\textquotesingle s Definition~7.2, including his convention for rational transforms.
reconstruction: The spectrum-containment and pole restrictions prevent an undefined rational calculus from being mistaken for a condition.
fate: \citet[Definitions~7.1--7.2]{davis1968shell} makes the quantifiers precise and explicitly traces the underlying spectral-set theory to earlier work.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Disk spectral sets are detected by spherical caps
notes: Theorem 2 says that, when \(\tau(X)\) is a spherical segment, \(X\) is spectral exactly when \(s(A)\subset\operatorname{conv}(\tau(X))\).
statement: For a closed linear relation in Davis\textquotesingle s sense and a closed generalized disk \(X\) in the Riemann sphere (a finite disk, a half-plane with infinity, or the exterior of an open disk with infinity), \[X\text{ is a spectral set}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s(\alpha)\subset\operatorname{conv}(\tau(X)).\] For bounded \(A\) and a finite disk \(X=\{z:|z-z_0|\leq r\}\), this is equivalently \(\|A-z_0I\|\leq r\). The spherical segment is a two-dimensional cap, not an arc.
reconstruction: The disk restriction is essential. The notebook does not claim this criterion for arbitrary closed spectral sets.
fate: Exact match: \citet[Theorem~7.2; preceding cases (i)--(iii)]{davis1968shell}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Finitely many smooth manifolds of torus homotopy type
notes: There are finitely many smooth manifolds of homotopy type \(T^n\), up to diffeomorphism.
statement: For each fixed \(n\geq5\), only finitely many diffeomorphism classes of closed connected smooth \(n\)-manifolds are homotopy equivalent to \(T^n=(S^1)^n\). This is a finiteness statement, not uniqueness in the smooth or PL category.
reconstruction: Closedness and the high-dimensional range are restored; the notebook is not evidence for a four-dimensional classification.
fate: \citet[Theorem~A]{hsiangshaneson1969fake}, communicated 6 January and published March 1969, gives PL finiteness. The passage to smooth finiteness is an additional deduction: on a fixed finite PL complex the smoothing choices and differences are controlled by finitely many cochains with finite sphere-smoothing groups, and concordant smoothings are diffeomorphic \citep[Theorems~1.1, 3.1, 4.2, 5.1]{hirsch1963obstruction}. The finiteness input is supplied by Kervaire--Milnor and the low-dimensional Cerf theorem \citep{kervairemilnor1963spheres,cerf1968gamma4}. Thus E uses these prior ingredients, not the PL theorem alone. The exact smooth statement is reported in \citet[p.~224, meeting of 22 April]{buchstabermishchenko1969tori}; that later meeting is confirmation, not evidence of prior publication. Subsequent topological uniqueness is \citet[main theorem]{hsiangwall1969tori}, received 14 May 1969. These dates distinguish prior results, the seminar exposition and later topological strengthening.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Simply connected finiteness with fixed characteristic data
notes: Novikov: homotopy type and Pontryagin classes determine a simply connected manifold up to finitely many possibilities.
statement: Fix a closed simply connected smooth manifold \(M^n\), \(n\geq5\). Among closed smooth \(N^n\) with an orientation-preserving homotopy equivalence \(f:N\to M\) satisfying \(p_i(N)=f^*p_i(M)\) in rational cohomology, there are only finitely many diffeomorphism types. Neither arbitrary fundamental groups nor dimension four are covered by this assertion.
reconstruction: The rational characteristic classes are compared under a specified homotopy equivalence. This does not say that the classes alone determine the homotopy type.
fate: \citet[Introduction and classification theorem, pp.~366--367]{novikov1964homotopy}, received 22 March 1963 and published 1964, develops the tangential homotopy classification; its finiteness consequence with rational Pontryagin data is also stated in the author\textquotesingle s research summary \citep[Topology]{novikov2014bibliography}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Homotopy spheres as the simply connected model
notes: Milnor\textquotesingle s sphere case is mentioned, with dimensions three and four marked unknown.
statement: For \(n\geq5\), the oriented diffeomorphism classes of smooth homotopy \(n\)-spheres form a finite abelian group \(\Theta_n\) under connected sum, identified with the corresponding oriented h-cobordism classes. The notebook\textquotesingle s historical uncertainty in low dimensions is not extended into an assertion about their present status.
reconstruction: Only the high-dimensional theorem needed in this talk is asserted; h-cobordism and diffeomorphism are separated before using the dimension hypothesis.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1.1--1.2]{kervairemilnor1963spheres}, received 19 April 1962 and published in May 1963, is the precise antecedent. The earlier companion occurrence 1966-92.2 treats the seven-dimensional example; this is a related exposition, not a new unresolved sphere problem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: h-cobordism
notes: Both \(M_i^n\subset W^{n+1}\) are deformation retracts and \(\partial W=M_1\cup M_2\).
statement: A smooth h-cobordism \((W;M_1,M_2)\) is a compact smooth cobordism whose two boundary inclusions are homotopy equivalences. For oriented manifolds the boundary convention is \(\partial W=M_1\sqcup(-M_2)\); collars make the inclusions cofibrations, so the homotopy-equivalence formulation is compatible with deformation retractions.
reconstruction: Compactness, collars and orientation signs are made explicit.
fate: This is the established framework in \citet[\S\S9,11]{milnor1966torsion}; the English survey appeared in 1966 and the checked Russian translation in 1967.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The s-cobordism classification
notes: Under Smale\textquotesingle s name, an h-cobordism is determined by one boundary and an invariant \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Wh}(\pi_1M_1)\).
statement: If \(M^n\) is closed and connected, \(n\geq5\), smooth h-cobordisms on \(M\), modulo diffeomorphism relative to the incoming boundary, are classified by their Whitehead torsion in \(\operatorname{Wh}(\pi_1M)\). In particular, torsion zero is equivalent to a product cobordism relative to that boundary.
reconstruction: Relative equivalence, dimension and the distinction from the simply connected h-cobordism theorem are restored.
fate: \citet[\S11, existence and uniqueness theorems]{milnor1966torsion} gives the classification. The non-simply-connected result is the s-cobordism theorem (Barden--Mazur--Stallings); attributing the full statement solely to Smale suppresses the essential extension.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Stable general linear groups, K1 and Whitehead groups
notes: The inductive general linear group is abelianized; \(\operatorname{Wh}\) is obtained by a further quotient. A noncommutative determinant is mentioned.
statement: For a unital ring \(R\), let \(GL(R)=\varinjlim_m GL_m(R)\) under \(A\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A,1)\), and let \(E(R)\) be the stable elementary subgroup. Then \(E(R)=[GL(R),GL(R)]\), \(K_1(R)=GL(R)/E(R)\), and \(\operatorname{Wh}(\pi)=K_1(\mathbb Z[\pi])/\langle[\pm g]:g\in\pi\rangle\). Dieudonn\'e\textquotesingle s determinant over a division ring is an analogy, not a literal determinant on an arbitrary group ring.
reconstruction: The ring-level and group-level Whitehead terminology is disambiguated, which is necessary for the next claim.
fate: \citet[\S1, Whitehead lemma; \S6]{milnor1966torsion} states these constructions before the talk.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The Whitehead group of a free abelian group vanishes
notes: The scan explicitly writes \(K_1(\mathbb Z+\cdots+\mathbb Z)=0\), with a gloss referring to the group ring, and attributes it to Bass.
statement: For \(\pi=\mathbb Z^n\), \(R=\mathbb Z[\pi]=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_n^{\pm1}]\), one has \(K_1(R)\simeq R^\times\simeq\{\pm1\}\times\mathbb Z^n\). Consequently \(\operatorname{Wh}(\mathbb Z^n)=0\), but \(K_1(R)\) is not zero.
reconstruction: The zero group is the Whitehead quotient. The plus signs denote a direct sum of infinite cyclic groups, not a direct sum of coefficient rings.
fate: Exact corrected theorem: \citet[p.~63, corollaries]{basshellerswan1964whitehead}, received 15 June 1963 and published 1964. Quotienting the surviving trivial units is the missing step.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Invertible polynomial and Laurent-polynomial matrices
notes: For polynomial matrices, invertibility is said to be equivalent to determinant \(\pm1\); elementary reduction after increasing size is discussed.
statement: Over the commutative polynomial ring \(\mathbb Z[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\), a square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is \(\pm1\). Over the group ring \(\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z^n]\), the units instead are \(\pm t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_n^{a_n}\), \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\). Stable elementary reduction detects the zero class in \(K_1\), and does not mean every invertible matrix already has determinant one.
reconstruction: The literal polynomial assertion is correct; applying it unchanged to the preceding Laurent group ring is not.
fate: The unit distinction and stable \(K_1\) calculation are precisely the setting of \citet[pp.~61--63]{basshellerswan1964whitehead}. The determinant criterion follows from the adjugate identity.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Stabilization at sufficiently large matrix size
notes: Bass: it suffices to restrict to matrices of sufficiently high order.
statement: For a commutative Noetherian ring \(R\) of finite Krull dimension, there exists a uniform \(m_0(R)\) such that every element of \(K_1(R)\) has a representative in \(GL_m(R)\) for every \(m\geq m_0(R)\). In particular this applies to \(\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_n^{\pm1}]\). This is a surjective stabilization statement; it does not by itself assert that every elementary equivalence is detected without further stabilization.
reconstruction: The ring hypotheses and uniform bound are restored; the weaker representability claim is all that the terse sentence needs. No unstated optimal bound or injectivity theorem is assigned to the speaker.
fate: The precise pre-existing result is \citet[Theorem~11.1 and Proposition~11.2(b)]{bass1964stable}. Immediately after that proposition Bass separately formulates injective stabilization as a conjecture; the two assertions must not be retroactively conflated.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Stable normal data under a homotopy equivalence
notes:
An embedding \(M^n\subset\mathbb R^N\) gives \(
u_M\), independent of the embedding stably; equivalence includes \(f^*
u_{M_2}=
u_{M_1}\).
statement: For a smooth embedding, \(TM\oplus\nu_M\cong\varepsilon^N\); thus the stable class \([\nu_M]-[\varepsilon^{N-n}]=-([TM]-[\varepsilon^n])\) is intrinsic. A tangential homotopy equivalence consists of a homotopy equivalence together with a stable identification of the pulled-back tangent, or equivalently normal, bundles.
reconstruction: Equality means stable bundle isomorphism over a specified map; it is stronger than equality of rational Pontryagin classes.
fate: These are the normal data used by \citet[Introduction and Ch.~I]{novikov1964homotopy}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Pontryagin classes and parallelizability of homotopy tori
notes: Adams\textquotesingle s J-functor and Novikov\textquotesingle s torus invariance are invoked; \(\nu_M=0\) is underlined.
statement: For a smooth homotopy torus in the high-dimensional range, the rational Pontryagin classes vanish, and the classification of fake tori supplies stable triviality of the normal bundle. These are distinct statements: vanishing of rational characteristic classes alone does not prove integral stable triviality for a general manifold.
reconstruction: The conclusion is separated from the abbreviated argument. No proof of stable triviality from rational classes alone is accepted.
fate: \citet[\S1]{novikov1966abelian} provides the relevant free-abelian and Pontryagin-class framework. The modern classification records parallelizability explicitly in \citet[p.~2212, Remark~1]{hambleton2006tori}. The notebook\textquotesingle s unnamed Adams reference is insufficient to identify a particular J-theorem with all its hypotheses.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Infinitely many manifolds with the homotopy type of S2 times S4
notes: \ru{на \(S^2\times S^4\) бесконечно много гладких структур}.
statement: There are infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic closed smooth manifolds homotopy equivalent to \(S^2\times S^4\), with different rational Pontryagin data. This must not be read as infinitely many smoothings of one fixed topological \(S^2\times S^4\). In dimension six that fixed topological-manifold smoothing problem has only finitely many possibilities.
reconstruction: On is interpreted as of the homotopy type of. The corrected meaning fits the surrounding comparison of characteristic classes.
fate: \citet[Introduction, consequences 1--2, pp.~208--209]{novikov1966abelian} explicitly distinguishes finiteness for a fixed simply connected topological manifold from infinitude within an appropriate homotopy type.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Pontryagin--Thom collapse and the degree-one fibre
notes: A tubular neighbourhood is collapsed to obtain \(S^N\to T_{\nu_M}\), whose Hurewicz image is \(+1\).
statement: An oriented embedding and tubular neighbourhood give a collapse \(c_M:S^N\to\operatorname{Th}(\nu_M)\). The Thom isomorphism sends the image of \([S^N]\) to \([M]\), so the Hurewicz image is the chosen generator of \(\widetilde H_N(\operatorname{Th}(\nu_M);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\). Homotopy-equivalent bases yield equivalent Thom spaces only when the relevant normal bundles have been identified stably over that equivalence.
reconstruction: The normal-bundle identification in the preceding page is retained; homotopy type of the base by itself is insufficient.
fate: This is the explicit method of \citet[pp.~366--367; Ch.~I, \S3]{novikov1964homotopy}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Stable torus splitting and finiteness of H inverse of one
notes: \(T_\nu(T^n)=\Sigma^{N-n}T^n=S^N\vee\bigvee_{i<N}S^i\); \(H^{-1}(1)\) is called a finite group and Serre is cited.
statement: For the trivial rank \(r=N-n\geq1\) bundle, \[\operatorname{Th}(\varepsilon^r_{T^n})\simeq\Sigma^r(T^n)_+\simeq\bigvee_{j=0}^n\bigvee^{\binom nj}S^{r+j}.\] Choose \(N>2n+1\) to lie in the stable range. The Hurewicz map \(\pi_N(\operatorname{Th}(\varepsilon^{N-n}_{T^n}))\to\mathbb Z\) is projection onto the top-sphere summand, with finite kernel because the other summands are positive stable stems. Its fibre over one is a finite torsor for that kernel, not a subgroup.
reconstruction: A disjoint basepoint, wedge multiplicities, stable-range choice and the affine nature of the fibre are supplied. The statement is restricted to the torus case, not all possible Thom spaces.
fate: The finite-fibre mechanism is already used in \citet[p.~366]{novikov1964homotopy}; Novikov invokes Serre\textquotesingle s homotopy-finiteness theorem. The classes-of-groups framework and sphere applications are developed in \citet[Chs.~I--IV]{serre1953classes}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: From normal cobordism to h-cobordism by surgery
notes: A homotopy between collapse maps produces a film; one must arrange retractions, classify films of finite index and use obstruction theory for modifications.
statement: A transverse homotopy of collapse maps with fixed normal data produces a normal cobordism. It need not be an h-cobordism. In dimensions at least five, surgery seeks to make the boundary inclusions homotopy equivalences; middle-dimensional surgery obstructions and the action on the structure set must be analyzed. Once an h-cobordism is obtained for fundamental group \(\mathbb Z^n\), its Whitehead torsion vanishes and the s-cobordism theorem makes it a product.
reconstruction: The missing surgery step is identified, not filled in as though the notebook contained a complete proof.
fate: The simply connected model is \citet[Ch.~I]{novikov1964homotopy}; the torus classification requires the non-simply-connected methods in \citet{hsiangshaneson1969fake}. The near-contemporary Buchstaber--Mishchenko abstract explicitly names Wall and Shaneson\textquotesingle s algebraic methods \citep[p.~224]{buchstabermishchenko1969tori}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: An equal-rank homogeneous complex manifold
notes: \(G\supset K\supset H\), \(\operatorname{rank}G=\operatorname{rank}K\); \(D=G/H\) is complex. The example is \(GL(2,\mathbb R)\), although \(G\) is called semisimple.
statement: Let \(G\) be a connected real semisimple group with finite centre, \(K\) a maximal compact subgroup and \(H\subset K\) a compact Cartan subgroup of \(G\). Equivalently the complex ranks of \(G\) and \(K\) agree. A choice of positive roots for \((\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C},\mathfrak h_{\mathbb C})\) determines an invariant integrable complex structure on \(D=G/H\), realized as an open flag-domain orbit. A valid rank-one example is \(SL(2,\mathbb R)/SO(2)\).
reconstruction: \(GL(2,\mathbb R)\) has a nontrivial central Lie algebra and is not semisimple. It is retained as a faithful notebook error, not silently read as \(SL_2\).
fate: The construction is established in \citet[\S\S1--2]{griffithsschmid1969locally}; that manuscript was received 3 April 1969, before the talk, assigned to Acta volume 123 (1969), and bears the print date 23 January 1970. The 1967 thesis and January 1968 announcement are distinct earlier stages \citep{schmid1968homogeneous}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The Weyl-group count concerns invariant structures
notes: The number of complex structures equals the number of Weyl-group elements.
statement: With a fixed compact Cartan and fixed identification of tangent root spaces, invariant integrable complex structures on \(G/H\) correspond to positive systems of the complex root system, hence there are \(|W|\) such marked structures. Passing to equivalence under diffeomorphisms or dropping invariance changes the counting problem.
reconstruction: The word invariant and the marking convention are necessary; this is not a count of all complex structures on the underlying smooth manifold.
fate: The positive-root construction is explicit in \citet[\S1]{griffithsschmid1969locally}; the Weyl group acts simply transitively on positive systems.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Homogeneous line bundles from Cartan characters
notes: \(\mathcal L_\lambda\) has fibre \(\mathbb C\); a one-dimensional representation of \(H\) determines it, with a Frobenius-reciprocity aside.
statement: An integral character \(\chi_\lambda:H\to U(1)\) gives \(\mathcal L_\lambda=G\times_H\mathbb C_{\chi_\lambda}\to G/H\), with the holomorphic structure fixed by the chosen positive system. Sections are equivariant functions, with \(f(gh)=\chi_\lambda(h)^{-1}f(g)\) for this associated-bundle convention. Induction and Frobenius reciprocity explain the representation-theoretic interpretation; arbitrary unintegrated Lie-algebra weights do not necessarily define a bundle on the given group.
reconstruction: Integrality and the bundle convention are stated explicitly; signs of highest weights depend on this convention.
fate: \citet[\S\S1,4]{griffithsschmid1969locally} treats the homogeneous bundle and its invariant Hermitian geometry.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Reduced L2 Dolbeault cohomology as harmonic forms
notes: Compactly supported \((0,i)\)-forms, \(\bar\partial\), its adjoint and \(\Box\) are introduced; \(\ker\Box=\mathcal H^i(\mathcal L_\lambda)\) is called i-dimensional cohomology.
statement: Choose invariant Hermitian metrics on \(G/H\) and \(\mathcal L_\lambda\). The complete homogeneous metric gives the closed \(L^2\) Dolbeault complex. In degree \(i\), reduced cohomology \(\ker\bar\partial_i/\overline{\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_{i-1}}\) is canonically the harmonic space \(\ker\Box_i\), where \(\Box=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial\) has its natural self-adjoint realization. The superscript is cohomological degree, not vector-space dimension.
reconstruction: The Hilbert completion is taken after the compactly supported test space; harmonic forms themselves are not required to have compact support. Reduced cohomology avoids silently assuming closed range.
fate: \citet[pp.~293--294, before Theorem~7.8]{griffithsschmid1969locally} defines the Hilbert space of harmonic forms and uses completeness. In the noncompact case a nonzero discrete-series realization is infinite-dimensional.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The compact specialization is Borel--Weil--Bott
notes: For compact \(G\), this is called the Borel--Weil theorem; Demazure is suggested as a reference.
statement: For compact connected semisimple \(G\), a homogeneous holomorphic line bundle on its complete flag manifold has zero cohomology in every degree when the shifted weight \(\lambda+\rho\) is singular. For a regular shifted weight, exactly one cohomological degree can be nonzero, and it realizes the finite-dimensional irreducible representation determined by the shifted Weyl action. Dominant weights in the degree-zero convention give Borel--Weil.
reconstruction: The compact higher-degree assertion is distinguished from the degree-zero Borel--Weil theorem; the sign convention is fixed by the bundle convention of the source.
fate: The full higher-cohomology statement is the pre-existing Borel--Weil--Bott theorem; \citet[Theorem~6.1]{griffithsschmid1969locally} recalls it. The notebook\textquotesingle s unspecific Demazure pointer is not converted into an invented bibliographic entry.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: Vanishing away from one degree for sufficiently regular weights
notes: Theorem 1 requires \(|(\lambda,\alpha)|>b\) for every simple root, and says \(\mathcal H^i=0\) except at \(k(\lambda+\rho)\).
statement: For the equal-rank flag domain with a fixed invariant metric, there is a constant \(b\) such that an integral weight satisfying \(|\langle\lambda,\alpha\rangle|>b\) for every root \(\alpha\) has harmonic \(L^2\) Dolbeault forms only in the degree \(q(\lambda+\rho)\). Enlarge \(b\) if necessary so that \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda+\rho\) lie in the same chamber. Conditions only on a fixed simple system with arbitrary signs do not ensure this distance from every wall.
reconstruction: Every-root regularity replaces the insufficient literal simple-root condition. Opposite large simple-root pairings can cancel on a nonsimple positive root.
fate: The exact all-chamber vanishing result is \citet[Theorem~7.8]{griffithsschmid1969locally}; the manuscript was received 3 April 1969 but printed 23 January 1970. Receipt alone is not evidence of public circulation. The January 1968 announcement \citep[p.~57]{schmid1968homogeneous} proves a restricted antecedent for sufficiently high powers of a bundle in a fixed antidominant chamber, not this full formulation. B records the later exact publication by Griffiths and Schmid, distinct from the irreducibility theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The remaining harmonic space realizes a discrete series
notes: In the exceptional degree, Theorem 1 identifies \(\mathcal H^{k(\lambda+\rho)}(\mathcal L_\lambda)\) with \(\pi_{\lambda+\rho}\), as a partial answer to Langlands.
statement: For sufficiently regular integral \(\lambda\) under the preceding hypotheses, the nonzero Hilbert representation of \(G\) on \(\mathcal H^{q(\lambda+\rho)}(\mathcal L_\lambda)\) is irreducible and is the discrete-series representation with Harish-Chandra parameter \(\lambda+\rho\), with the weight convention of the chosen holomorphic bundle.
reconstruction: The theorem is the precise first conjecture component recoverable from the notes. The full all-weights formulation in the problem index is identified from the cited literature, not quoted as notebook text.
fate: \citet[Introduction, p.~255]{griffithsschmid1969locally} announces Schmid\textquotesingle s proof after completion of that manuscript; the full paper is \citet{schmid1971langlands}. \citet[\S3, Theorem~2]{schiffmann1971borel} states exactly the sufficiently regular result. The unrestricted harmonic realization is proved in \citet{schmid1976l2}, as explicitly confirmed in the author\textquotesingle s 1978 ICM address, published in 1980, p.~204 \citep{schmid1980representations}; the 1971 paper alone is not credited with the unrestricted theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026: this sufficiently regular realization is established; the general Langlands harmonic realization was proved by Schmid in 1976. No remaining open subproblem is inferred from this occurrence.

title: The cohomological degree counts signed positive roots
notes: Theorem 2 writes \(K(\mu)\) but uses \(\lambda\) on the right, counting compact roots with negative pairing and noncompact roots with positive pairing.
statement: For a regular parameter \(\mu\), with positive roots partitioned as \(\Delta_c^+\sqcup\Delta_n^+\), \[q(\mu)=\#\{\alpha\in\Delta_c^+:\langle\mu,\alpha\rangle<0\}+\#\{\beta\in\Delta_n^+:\langle\mu,\beta\rangle>0\}.\] In the preceding realization use \(\mu=\lambda+\rho\). Counting both signs of every root would give a different, generally constant count.
reconstruction: The variable is made uniform and positive roots are specified. These changes are faithful-error emendations because the scan agrees with the transcription.
fate: The root-count convention already occurs in \citet[\S2, eq.~(2.1), p.~415]{griffiths1966locally}, followed by compact-quotient cohomology in \S3; it predates this talk. The precise later discrete-series convention is recorded in \citet[\S3, before Theorem~1]{schiffmann1971borel}; compare \citet[\S7]{griffithsschmid1969locally}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: The unspecified decay-at-infinity comparison
notes: \ru{Если с убыванием на бесконечности --- будут те же когомологии}.
statement: No exact comparison theorem is determined without a specified decay space, its topology, the closed extension of \(\bar\partial\), and the meaning of same cohomology. Harmonic \(L^2\), smooth Dolbeault, compactly supported and rapidly decreasing cohomology are different constructions and cannot simply be identified.
reconstruction: The possible function-space interpretations are alternatives, not silently supplied hypotheses.
fate: \citet[p.~293 and Introduction, p.~255]{griffithsschmid1969locally} explicitly treats comparison with ordinary cohomology as a separate issue; it does not validate every possible reading of this sentence. The notes leave the second Langlands conjecture similarly unnamed at formula level.
present_status: As of November 2026: the exact assertion in this sentence remains unidentified from the surviving wording; this is an evidential limit, not a claim that a definite mathematical problem is open.

title: Finitely many h-cobordism classes of homotopy tori
notes: Manifolds of the homotopy type of a torus are divided into finitely many classes by h-cobordisms.
statement: For each fixed \(n\geq5\), the closed connected smooth manifolds homotopy equivalent to \(T^n\) comprise finitely many smooth h-cobordism classes. The dimension, smooth category and unmarked equivalence relation are essential to this reading.
reconstruction: The same high-dimensional, closed-manifold setting is carried over from the preceding lecture.
fate: This follows from the PL classification of \citet[Theorem~A]{hsiangshaneson1969fake} together with the finite-smoothing deduction made explicit at occurrence 1968-171.1. It is not the PL theorem alone. The exact Moscow report is \citet[p.~224]{buchstabermishchenko1969tori}, from the following day, 22 April 1969.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.

title: How many diffeomorphism types occur in one h-cobordism class?
notes: \ru{Задача: показ., что в \(\forall\) классе конечн. число}.
statement: Given a closed smooth homotopy \(n\)-torus, \(n\geq5\), prove that its smooth h-cobordism class contains only finitely many diffeomorphism types. In fact it contains exactly one: every h-cobordism has torsion in \(\operatorname{Wh}(\mathbb Z^n)=0\), and hence is a product by the s-cobordism theorem.
reconstruction: Up to diffeomorphism is restored from record 171. The conclusion concerns unmarked boundary manifolds, not equality of all markings or parametrizations.
fate: The two ingredients already predate the question: \citet[p.~63]{basshellerswan1964whitehead} and \citet[\S11]{milnor1966torsion}. Thus the question is a proof step in an exposition, not a remaining open problem.
present_status: As of November 2026: resolved in the stated high-dimensional smooth setting, with exactly one diffeomorphism type per h-cobordism class.

title: Morse modifications of cobordisms
notes: The simplest films are classified by Morse modifications.
statement: A relative Morse function on a compact smooth cobordism gives a handle decomposition. Handle additions, slides and cancellation are the geometric operations used to simplify the relative chain complex and expose Whitehead torsion. The notebook does not give a new finite algorithm classifying arbitrary cobordisms.
reconstruction: The brief method label is expanded only to the standard handle-theoretic interpretation needed for the preceding problem.
fate: This is the established method in \citet[\S\S9,11]{milnor1966torsion}.
present_status: As of November 2026: established in the stated scope; this occurrence does not pose an unresolved problem.
